evidence_spans: the feasibility of laser-based additive manufacturing of the refractory metal high entropy alloy W 20 Mo 20 Ta 20 Nb 20 V 20 by laser powder bed fusion (PBF-LB/M) is investigated in the present work.
In-situ alloy formation from mixtures of easily available elemental powders is employed

It is shown that PBF-LB/M of W 20 Mo 20 Ta 20 Nb 20 V 20 is in general possible and that a complete fusion of the powder mixture without a significant number of undissolved particles is achievable by in-situ alloy formation during PBF-LB/M when selecting favorable process parameter combinations.

questions.why_it_matters: The trigger cites a general mechanism of undissolved particles, and the text notes set B has fewer but still has undissolved particles. Knowing the exact boundary condition where undissolved particles disappear is critical for process optimization and validating the 'complete fusion' claim.
questions.known_context: Set B has higher energy density (889 J/mm3) and smaller powder size than Set A, yet undissolved particles remain (though fewer). Set A has more undissolved particles but fewer cracks. The Abstract claims complete fusion is achievable with favorable parameters.
questions.unresolved_information: The specific parameter window (energy density, scan speed) where undissolved W particles are eliminated in the W20Mo20Ta20Nb20V20 system, distinct from the cited Mo/Ti system.
evidence_spans: While the sample built with parameter set PBF-LB/M B contains less undissolved particles, parameter set PBF-LB/M A is superior to PBF-LB/M B in terms of cracking.

questions.question: Does the 'parameter dependence of the amount of remaining high melting particles' cited in the text ([32]) manifest as a monotonic decrease in undissolved W particles with increasing volumetric energy density in the W-Mo-Ta-Nb-V system, or are there competing factors (e.g., evaporation of V) that create a non-linear relationship between energy input and particle dissolution?
questions.why_it_matters: Understanding the mechanism (monotonic vs. complex) is essential to distinguish between simple melting issues and complex thermo-chemical interactions (like V evaporation mentioned in Methods) affecting the final microstructure.
questions.known_context: The text cites Yadroitsev [42] regarding Mo in Ti, Fischer [43] regarding Nb in Ti, and [32] regarding parameter dependence. It also notes V evaporation compensation. Set B (higher energy) has fewer undissolved particles than A.
questions.unresolved_information: Whether the relationship is strictly monotonic with energy or if there is a limit or competing effect, specifically for the W-based system in this paper.
evidence_spans: However, they also reported a parameter dependence of the amount of remaining high melting particles.

research_thread.scientific_problem: Achieving complete fusion of high-melting elements (W, Ta) in refractory metal high entropy alloys (W-Mo-Ta-Nb-V) via PBF-LB/M without introducing defects like cracks, while balancing process parameters.
research_thread.material_system: Refractory Metal High Entropy Alloy: W20Mo20Ta20Nb20V20
research_thread.sample_lineage: PBF-LB/M samples fabricated using two parameter sets (A: low energy, large hatch; B: high energy, small hatch) from elemental powder mixtures with pre-compensated Vanadium.
research_thread.intervention: Varying PBF-LB/M process parameters (laser power, scan speed, hatch distance) to alter volumetric energy density and heat input.
research_thread.baseline: Standard in-situ alloy formation challenges with high melting point elements leading to undissolved particles.

evidence_spans: E.g., Yadroitsev et al. [ [42] ] report undissolved Mo particles in Ti-alloys produced by in-situ alloy formation and PBF-LB/M while the lower melting Cu was completely dissolved in the Ti-matrix.
PBF-LB/M A results in considerably smaller cracks than PBF-LB/M B but contains undissolved powder particles which were identified as tungsten particles by EDS measurements.
While the sample built with parameter set PBF-LB/M B contains less undissolved particles, parameter set PBF-LB/M A is superior to PBF-LB/M B in terms of cracking.

The low laser power/low scan speed parameter set PBF-LB/M B was furthermore derived from previous work on in-situ alloy formation strategies with high melting particles and is assumed to support dissolution of W in the meltpool [ [32] ].
For the high-melting elements W and Ta a smaller D 90 (23.1 µm and 36.1 µm respectively) was chosen to ease fusion during PBF-LB/M and to avoid undissolved particles.
